newsitem.title: USA: NIMO says likely to appeal FERC rule on NYPA pact.
newsitem.headline: NIMO says likely to appeal FERC rule on NYPA pact.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp (NIMO) said Thursday it will likely appeal a decision by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) that temporarily halted its planned cancellation of a power contract with the New York Power Authority (NYPA).
"We likely will (appeal). We do believe our decision is right to terminate the contract," said NIMO spokeswoman Kerry Burns.

FERC ruled Wednesday that while it will hold hearings on the dispute, NIMO must continue delivering NYPA electricity to six companies for at least five months and begin delivery service to Cascades Niagara Falls Inc, a manufacturer of recycled paper products.
Burns did not give a date when NIMO would file its appeal.

NIMO argued the two-part supply agreement with NYPA is uneconomic because it requires NIMO to buy electricity from NYPA's Fitzpatrick nuclear power plant at above-market prices and wheel additional power from the plant to upstate industrial customers.
NIMO asked FERC for permission to stop delivery of high-load-factor power to NYPA business customers in its service territory effective May 24.
In lieu of power from NYPA, NIMO proposed supplying electricity to the customers at a price below what they are now paying NYPA.
